decisions.evidence: Band1, Modim line 2 (the line starting לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד): both words show a full-height vav between ד and ר. Each is a real vertical stroke, not a lone dot over ד. The full page shows the same thing.
Band1, start of Modim line 3: shva under ל and qamatz in final ך. I see no dot inside the ל, on either the band or the full page.

Band2, centered וּכְתוֹב line: the ב of בריתך has an inner dot like the one in בְּנֵי next to it, and a colon follows. The source prints dagesh after בני, which is grammatically unusual. Keep it literally. A sic/corr to בְרִיתֶךָ is optional; do not change the base text silently.
Band2, Sim Shalom line 2: there is no dot or other mark between עַמֶּךָ and בָּרְכֵנוּ. The period belongs only in the English (s123 'Thy people. Bless'). It cannot be carried over to the Hebrew.

Band2, Sim Shalom line 3, after נָתַתָּ: there may be a speck inside the ל, but at this resolution I can't tell a dagesh from ink noise. The full page doesn't settle it. Needs a higher-zoom crop of this word.
Band3, Elohai Netzor line 2: two dots stacked vertically (sof pasuq/colon) before פְּתַח. This is clearly not a single period. The full page agrees.
s123 band2: 'of our salvation and of our aid, Selah!' The mark after 'aid' has a comma tail.

remaining_uncertainties.evidence: Band1 line 1: a three-dot cluster under ז fits segol. It is crowded next to the hataf segol under ח but readable. Probably segol; I would not mark it as a problem.
There is a faint dot in the yod in both places. It is too faint to confirm at band resolution. Isolate it as faint.
Band1, Modim line 1: the mark under ש has a T shape (qamatz), not a segol. Keep the source form. A sic/corr to שָׁאַתָּה is optional, but don't normalize it silently.
Band1 line 4: there is a short raised stroke between כל and יום, consistent with a maqaf. The words are run together, but the stroke appears present. Medium confidence.
The dot is faint but appears present inside the פ. Isolate it as faint.
Band2: I can't confirm a dot above the left edge of כ at this resolution. Faint or absent. Do not supply it from memory.
There is a small apostrophe-like stroke after the א. It may be a print accent or an artifact. Do not add or drop it without a zoomed crop.
Band2 line 3 start: possible inner dot, not clearly resolved. Faint.
A small vertical stroke appears next to the patah under א. It looks like a meteg hosted on א, but this is low certainty.
Band3 line 2: I don't see a clear dot in ת. Keep it unpointed unless a zoom shows one.
Band3 line 3: the qamatz is faint but its shape is visible. Probably present.

notes: Confirmed from pixels: the first עַל before חַיֵּינוּ has no vav. וּבְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ is spelled defectively (מצותיך, holam vav, no yod after ו). Sim Shalom ends with a period after בִּשְׁלוֹמֶךָ, not sof pasuq. בְּסֵפֶר is not indented. וּכְתוֹב is centered.
s122 ends with מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם followed by a printed period. The continuation is on the next scan.
s123: 'O Lord who makes peace.' has no comma after Lord in the print. Keep it literally. A comma is only a sic/corr candidate. 'All-benevolent' has a real mid-line hyphen, so keep it.
